BER-RENT-02.reason: Same rent-control law/category as BER-RENT-01. This record mainly describes coverage/exemptions for Berkeley’s rent ordinance, while BER-RENT-01 better states the main operative rent-increase requirement. Coverage/exemption provisions are part of the same law and should be merged into one kept record per law per category.

BER-JC-02.reason: Relocation assistance for owner move-in and Ellis evictions is part of Berkeley's just-cause eviction regime and annual adjustment of payment amounts. Under the duplicate rule, relocation/implementation provisions of the same law should be merged into the main just-cause record.

BOS-JC-01.reason: This ordinance requires a tenant-rights/resources notice and city filing when serving a notice to quit or non-renewal, but it expressly does not limit the grounds for eviction or non-renewal. In just_cause_eviction, notice provisions are operative only when part of a just-cause regime; here it is a procedural notice tied to eviction, not a cause limitation.

CA-DEP-02.reason: This record mainly states that application screening fees are not security deposits and are governed by the separate application-screening-fee statute; it does not itself impose an operative security-deposit rule.

CA-SCR-01.reason: Main operative subject is application screening fee caps and procedures, not screening restrictions such as criminal-history or source-of-income limits. Timing/availability conditions here are part of the fee statute and are better kept in application_screening_fees.

HOB-JC-01.reason: This record only defines 'just cause for eviction' by cross-reference to New Jersey state law and does not itself provide operative local causes, notice, coverage, or relocation rules in this category.

LA-RENT-P02.reason: This motion concerns possible regulation of algorithm-based rent-setting software, not an operative rent increase limit or rent-control/preemption rule in this category.

LA-JC-03.reason: These occupant protections govern a specific no-fault demolition/new-construction eviction scenario under the same city just-cause/resident-protection law framework; keep the broader record covering the main operative just-cause rule.

LA-ALG-P01.reason: The motion only orders a study/report on possible future restrictions and does not itself create an operative algorithmic rent-setting rule, prohibition, definition, penalty, or effective date.

MA-RENT-P04.reason: This pending bill's subject is algorithmic rent setting, not rent increase limits, and the record itself says no substantive rent-cap rule can be extracted.

MA-RENT-P03.reason: This pending bill concerns algorithmic rent fixing rather than rent increase limits, and no operative rent-cap or local rent-control rule is provided here.

SD-ALG-01.reason: Same law as the enacted municipal code provisions on algorithmic rent-setting; this ordinance record is another citation/version of the same enacted measure, and the code record better states the operative rule.

SF-JC-02.reason: Relocation payment amounts for specified no-fault evictions are part of the same just-cause eviction law and are ancillary to the main operative just-cause rule already captured in SF-JC-01.

SF-DEP-01.reason: This record gives only the annual interest rate on security deposits and expressly lacks any maximum deposit amount; it does not state an operative security-deposit cap or comparable rule for this category.
